counts_closing_quote: All in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 1343.

forfeiture.notes: If convicted of any of Counts 1-4, forfeiture of proceeds-traceable property; substitute-asset allegation under § 853(p). No dollar amount is stated in the forfeiture paragraphs.

amounts.quote: In all, between approximately July 2020 and June 2025, Faladcare submitted reimbursement claims totaling over $2.2 million.
amounts.notes: Face language is submitted reimbursement claims totaling over $2.2 million (amount_billed), not amount_paid and not proven_loss. Do not add to Aden Brilliant Minds $2.3M or FOF $250M.

amounts.quote: From those locations, the FALADES claimed to service about 100 different beneficiaries and for such services claimed to be entitled to over $2.2 million.
amounts.notes: Same >$2.2M as para 13; do not sum. Indictment alleges operations provided only a fraction of that claimed total and that proceeds were diverted to conspirators including Faladcare employees. No personal-pocketing dollar figure is stated on the face of this indictment.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Consultants could bill Medicaid about $174 for a consulting session.
program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.notes: Statewide HSS rate recital, identical boilerplate to Aden indictment.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Providers can bill about $68 per hour of transition services provided.
Moving expenses of up to $3,000, subject to conditions.
Before the Program’s inaugural year, DHS predicted the Program would cost about $2.6 million annually.

statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.quote: In 2021 alone, the Program paid out more than $21 million in claims. That figure ballooned in the following years: $42 million in 2022, $74 million in 2023, $104 million in 2024. In just the first six months of 2025, the Program paid out another $61 million.
statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.notes: Statewide HSS program_spend recitals, not Falade alleged_loss. Identical boilerplate in the Aden indictment. Do not add to Faladcare >$2.2M, Aden $2.3M, or FOF $250M.

other_face_facts: Para 11: Christopher Falade is the father of Emmanuel Falade; they worked together to operate Faladcare Inc. within the HSS Program.
Para 12: Faladcare was paid at quarter-hourly rates with Medicaid dollars based on services it claimed to have provided (paid language, no dollar).
Para 16: purported to service individuals from business offices in Little Canada and Woodbury, Minnesota.
Para 17: diversion of fraud proceeds to conspirators including Faladcare employees — no dollar stated.
Count 4 names HealthPartners as the email recipient.
do_not: Do not add Falade billed dollars to Aden Brilliant Minds $2.3M, Aden personal-pocketing, or FOF $250M.
Do not invent an Aden-style personal-pocketing figure for Falade; none appears on this indictment.
